LESSON: DANCE

Grade: PP2
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: PERFORMANCE
Topic 8.1: Dance

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Dance. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. respond to changes in • Guide learners to observe tempo and rhythms a variety of dance. through body • Guide learners to respond movement for to tempo and rhythms enjoyment through body movement

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: DANCE
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Dance helps you succeed in PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: DANCE
Study Dance like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Respond to changes in • Guide learners to observe tempo and rhythms a variety of dance. through body • Guide learners to respond movement for to tempo and rhythms enjoyment through body movement

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to changes in • Guide learners to observe tempo and rhythms a variety of dance. through body • Guide learners to respond movement for to tempo and rhythms enjoyment through body movement. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to changes in • Guide learners to observe tempo and rhythms a variety of dance. through body • Guide learners to respond movement for to tempo and rhythms enjoyment through body movement.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Dance” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to changes in • Guide learners to observe tempo and rhythms a variety of dance. through body • Guide learners to respond movement for to tempo and rhythms enjoyment through body movement. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Dance is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Dance” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: respond to changes in • Guide learners to observe tempo and rhythms a variety of dance. through body • Guide learners to respond movement for to tempo and rhythms enjoyment through body movement)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Dance to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: respond to changes in • Guide learners to observe tempo and rhythms a variety of dance. through body • Guide learners to respond movement for to tempo and rhythms enjoyment through body movement.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Dance from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Dance: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Dance?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which dancing style do you 5 Lessons strand the learner should freely in pairs, small love most?
2. Which costumes would you use dancing style for to watch a video clip on while dancing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Dance means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: respond to changes in • Guide learners to observe tempo and rhythms a variety of dance. through body • Guide learners to respond movement for to tempo and rhythms enjoyment through body movement.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
